clue.text: Plant nibbled by small owlet

indicators.note: the plant is taken out of the words small owlet, a bite from the middle of them

explanation.surface: A tiny young owl pecks at a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallow is a flowering herb of the hollyhock family.

clue.text: Driving car, doctor has to make phone call

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to give someone a ring is to telephone them

explanation.surface: A doctor at the wheel has to pull over and make a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'make' only join the pieces; 'to' is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoring is the activity of travelling by automobile.

clue.text: Play to review when worked up?

parts.note: to look back at something is to review it
worked up means angry, so in anger

explanation.surface: A drama critic revisits a show in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is John Osborne's 1956 drama, which gave its name to the 'angry young men' writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Osborne's kitchen-sink drama is a famous stage work of 1950s Britain.

clue.text: Is introduced by newspaper editor as arranged

indicators.note: the word is is brought in between the paper and its editor

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical serving a party or cause
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor gets something sorted and printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something organised has been put in order, planned.

clue.text: Scored without getting excited?

explanation.surface: A sports report on a calm goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer has written (scored) music; someone collected keeps calm and unflustered.

clue.text: Water nymph provided aid once at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of aid and once are mixed up

explanation.surface: A water nymph once lent a hand out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Oceanids were sea nymphs, daughters of Oceanus.

clue.text: Old man consumes endless Italian wine and food

indicators.note: the father swallows the wine, so it goes inside him

parts.note: old man is slang for father, PA

indicators.note: the last letter of the wine's name is lopped off

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont

explanation.surface: Dad tucks into wine and an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ASTI to AST, which PA surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta, such as spaghetti, is a staple food made from dough.

clue.text: Fashion designer N disconcerted by cat enters calmly

indicators.note: the letters of the following phrase are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A designer is unsettled when a cat strolls coolly into the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'N' in the held clue is a stray mark from scanning, with no job.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella McCartney is a British couturier, daughter of Paul McCartney.

clue.text: Dance move one's taken up during parties

indicators.note: the turned word sits in the middle of the two parties

parts.note: a do is a party, and parties gives two of them

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means written bottom to top

parts.note: one's is one is, I + S

explanation.surface: Someone is swept up into the fun at a round of parties.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' reads upwards, and 'one's' is short for 'one is'. A do-si-do comes from square dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-si-do is a square-dance figure where partners circle back to back.

clue.text: Workforce on a N A Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, so the a follows the staff

parts.note: the staff are the workforce of an organisation

explanation.surface: Workers posted to a remote Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'N A' in the held clue are stray scanning marks. Staffa is the island west of Mull with Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small uninhabited isle of the Inner Hebrides.

clue.text: Such lack of consideration unlikely among philosophers

definitions.text: Such lack of consideration unlikely among philosophers

parts.words: Such lack of consideration unlikely among philosophers
parts.note: people who think for a living would hardly be found lacking in thought, so the clue reads the word as an absence of thinking as well as of care

explanation.surface: A remark that philosophers are seldom inconsiderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderateness literally means being without thinking about others.

clue.text: Wrongly take in Christmas visitor?

parts.note: to rob is to take something unlawfully
taken as written

explanation.surface: A burglar sneaking in at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The visitor is the red-breasted bird seen on British Christmas cards, not a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: The redbreast is a garden bird pictured on festive cards in Britain.

clue.text: Like some birds pursued by admirer

indicators.note: pursued by the fan means the fan comes in front of the following

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A celebrity is followed everywhere by a devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeons and some flycatchers have tails that spread like a fan.

clue.text: Capital one invested in failing casino

indicators.note: one is put inside the shuffled letters, as money goes into a business
a failing casino is collapsing, so its letters fall apart and rearrange

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Money is sunk into a gambling house going under.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Maiden walked round, about to leave

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the whole is read backwards
walked goes round the maiden, enclosing it

parts.note: paced means walked
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl strolls about before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts M inside PACED to make PMACED, and 'about' reverses that. In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly or secretly.

clue.text: Woman taking A opposing position?

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A woman takes the contrary view in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' in the held clue is a stray scanning mark. 'taking' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female given name.

clue.text: De Gaulle's refusal to receive a European leader, once

indicators.note: the French no takes in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: the French president would say non for no
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: De Gaulle famously said no to letting a European in.
explanation.walkthrough: De Gaulle twice vetoed Britain's entry to the European Community, which the surface recalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was emperor of France in the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Oscar's right for film director

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: An Academy Award is fitting for a moviemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award; it is the writer Oscar Wilde. Billy Wilder directed Some Like It Hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder was an Austrian-American Hollywood moviemaker.

clue.text: Defeat in east: nothing unusual in that?

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A war correspondent shrugs at yet another defeat on the eastern front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something routine is ordinary, everyday, part of the normal course.

clue.text: In Pennsylvania, North America, find brilliant cure for illness

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

indicators.note: brilliant is placed in North America, splitting its two letters

parts.note: ace means excellent, brilliant

explanation.surface: An American miracle cure is discovered in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for all ills.

clue.text: Quite attractive

explanation.surface: A lukewarm compliment on someone's looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can mean fairly or rather; as an adjective it means good-looking.

clue.text: Male name, one adopted by Greek actor

indicators.note: one is taken in by the other pieces, as a child is taken into a family

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer
A means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A child is taken in by a Greek performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham is a common boy's given name.

clue.text: Odour has spread to English pub

indicators.note: a smell that has spread is scattered, so its letters disperse

explanation.surface: A smell has drifted into an English inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges ODOURHAS into ROADHOUS, before E.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or bar on a main road.

clue.text: Detective, say, returns instinctively to abode

indicators.note: say means spoken, the detective's name pronounced

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes, Conan Doyle's fictional sleuth of Baker Street

explanation.surface: A detective goes back home by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes is said with a silent L, so it sounds like the entered word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon homes when it flies back to its base unaided.

clue.text: Trunk must be carried by actors occasionally

indicators.note: the word sits inside the two following words, carried within them

explanation.surface: Actors now and then have to haul a big chest about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a travelling chest the actors carry; it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: New fitting in faulty heating machine needing lots of attention

indicators.note: the new letter is fitted into the rearranged letters
a faulty machine is out of order, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A repair fitting a new part to a broken heater.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something high-maintenance demands constant care.

clue.text: Communists, so to speak, who hit the target?

indicators.note: the words are to be heard, said out loud

parts.note: followers of Karl Marx, Marx men

explanation.surface: A comment that Marxists always score a bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack shots are skilled at striking what they aim at.

clue.text: African fellow joined by American briefly

parts.note: Ken is a man's name, a fellow

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, the final letter dropped

parts.note: a Yank is an American

explanation.surface: An African man teams up with an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a citizen of Kenya in East Africa.
